head: Complex dependence on catalyst operation history

head: d-Band Center Positions
snippet: The d-band theory is widely used to analyze and predict the catalytic performance of materials. Based on the assumption that the d-orbitals of metals directly interact with antibonding orbitals of reaction intermediates, the d-band center position is considered to be a key parameter in evaluating catalytic activity. [64, 65] The d-band center position of binary alloys is reported to be controlled by varying the constituent atoms and their concentration in the alloy. For instance, Au-Pt alloys show an almost linear positive shift of the d-band center from 0 to 0.15 eV for Pt atoms as the concentration of Au increases.

head: Potential-dependent SERS background signal
snippet: A strong background in the Raman spectra complicates the interpretation of specific SERS bands and their intensities seriously. The background intensity depends on the The Journal of Chemical Physics ARTICLE scitation.org/journal/jcp electric potential as well as the "history" of the surface, e.g., the sequence and duration of the previously applied potential steps. The magnitude of the SERS backgrounds correlates with the strength of the Raman enhancement effect. Therefore, aside from background subtraction also appropriate normalization of the Raman intensities is advisable, which possibly has not been considered in the previous operando SERS studies on CO 2 RR.
